title: Bound cumulative source retrieval in Polaris
request: Implement the reviewed miniLLM retrieval-budget change and retain a structured proposal so the actual diff can be reviewed in Proposal Nav.

overview.summary: Implemented an opt-in per-run source-character budget in Polaris. Controller admits read/search results before retaining them in history; a pure helper trims source without charging metadata. The CLI accepts --max-source-chars, and None preserves prior behavior. This review shows the actual five-file diff against captured pre-edit working-tree files, not against a potentially different Git HEAD. All 37 offline Polaris tests passed in the staged implementation.
overview.architecture: This repository contains two related runtimes. polaris is the small async, read-only runtime: __main__.py composes Config, model, Workspace, and Controller; controller.py owns execution policy, history, deadlines, and dispatch; tools.py owns argument validation and bounded descriptor-relative filesystem access; model.py converts provider-neutral messages into Ollama requests. The separate simple_agent coding runtime already has a controller-side retrieval budget but different state and observation formats. Use it as design evidence, not as an imported dependency. Several simple_agent files have uncommitted changes; this proposal deliberately targets the unchanged Polaris code and new files.
questions: The implementation remains opt-in. Should a default allowance be enabled after representative workload measurements?

annotations.title: Declare the per-run retrieval allowance
annotations.intent: Add max_source_chars: int | None = None after the existing Config fields. Validate that a configured value is a strictly positive integer, rejecting booleans. Keep None as the default so existing Config calls, tool payloads, and CLI behavior remain unchanged until the option is enabled.
annotations.rationale: Config already owns per-run decision, time, and tool-call limits. A cumulative retrieval allowance is another execution policy, rather than a model setting or filesystem permission. Adding the field at the end preserves the current positional constructor.
alternatives: Changing Workspace.MAX_BYTES would only shrink each individual read; repeated reads would still accumulate in history.
An enabled default could be useful later, but choosing one before measuring typical workloads would change existing behavior. Start opt-in.

annotations.title: Add a pure source-admission helper
annotations.intent: Introduce admit_source(tool_name, observation, remaining_chars), returning a copied observation, admitted-character count, and whether budget trimming occurred. For read_file, admit its text field; for search_files, admit match text in result order, truncating a final excerpt and omitting later source excerpts when necessary. Count decoded Python string characters, including whitespace and repeated retrievals. Preserve line/path metadata and existing truncation flags. A zero allowance returns empty source with truncated=true. Other tool payloads pass through without charge.
annotations.rationale: This transformation is deterministic and independent of model transport, filesystem I/O, and run state. A separate pure helper can be tested with small dictionaries. The coding agent already demonstrates source-only accounting, but its helper expects a different envelope and coding-agent state/policy objects; importing it would couple the two runtimes.
alternatives: Place all trimming inline in Controller.run, at the cost of mixing payload transformation with scheduling and failure handling.
Extract one shared budget library for polaris and simple_agent. That is a broader migration across different observation formats and should be a separate proposal.

annotations.title: Initialize accounting for each execution
annotations.intent: Initialize consumed_source_chars to zero inside run, alongside the per-execution deadline and cancellation state. Consult Config.max_source_chars to determine whether admission is enabled. Do not store consumption on Controller, Workspace, or the model instance.
annotations.rationale: Controller owns the lifetime of one execution and constructs its fresh history. Local accounting resets when the same controller is reused and does not leak allowance between runs. Workspace continues to enforce its independent access and per-file bounds.
alternatives: Store consumption on Workspace, which would incorrectly associate a run budget with a potentially shared filesystem capability.
Store a mutable counter on Config or Controller, which would need explicit reset and concurrency rules.

annotations.title: Apply the allowance before retaining source
annotations.intent: After a successful built-in source tool result, and before JSON encoding, apply the admission helper when the budget is configured. Compute remaining allowance from the run-local counter and increment it only by admitted source characters. Preserve the existing ok/result envelope and add bounded context_budget metadata for these source observations: limit_chars, consumed_chars, remaining_chars, and truncated_by_budget. Do not charge JSON labels or tool errors. Keep final answers and non-source tools available at exhaustion. With None, preserve the exact previous observation shape. Preserve cancellation checks and the existing tool_error path. This caps admitted source, not filesystem reads or the complete model token window.
annotations.rationale: This is the shared boundary immediately before source enters history and future model requests. The current run appends each serialized result to history, and every next decision receives a deep copy of that history. Enforcing here covers repeated reads and mixed read/search batches, independently of the Ollama adapter.
alternatives: Trim only inside OllamaModel.decide. That would leave the controller history and programmatic results growing, and other model implementations could bypass it.
Stop the run as soon as allowance reaches zero. That would prevent the model from producing a final answer from the evidence already admitted.

annotations.title: Forward the CLI setting into Config
annotations.intent: Pass max_source_chars to Config as a keyword argument, leaving the existing positional arguments intact. Use getattr(args, "max_source_chars", None) so older programmatic Namespace callers and the existing CLI redaction test keep working when they omit the new option. Continue using the current structured setup_error response for invalid configuration.
annotations.rationale: The CLI is the composition boundary that translates parsed user options into runtime configuration. The model constructor and tool registry do not need awareness of the retrieval budget.
alternatives: Read an environment variable directly in Controller.run, which would hide policy from programmatic callers and make independent tests harder.

annotations.title: Expose an optional terminal flag
annotations.intent: Add --max-source-chars with type=int and default=None. Explain in help that it limits cumulative admitted source characters per run, not bytes or model tokens, and is disabled when omitted. Show an offline mock command in documentation; no credentials are needed to exercise the policy with scripted decisions.
annotations.rationale: User-facing option parsing belongs beside the other execution limits. Core Config validation remains authoritative for both CLI and programmatic use, and the same option applies to mock and cloud runs.
alternatives: Use a provider-specific token limit here. Tokenization varies across models and would turn this deterministic, provider-neutral allowance into a model-dependent policy.

annotations.title: Cover source admission and run isolation
annotations.intent: Add offline unittest coverage using temporary workspaces and MockModel: disabled-budget compatibility; exact and partial boundaries; repeated reads charged again; a mixed read/search batch sharing one allowance; Unicode counted as characters; metadata excluded; existing truncated=true retained; tool errors uncharged; and allowance reset when a Controller instance runs twice. Assert that the next recorded model request contains only admitted text. Verify completion remains possible at zero allowance. Add Config rejection cases and a Namespace-based CLI forwarding case. Keep all credentials and network calls out of these tests.
annotations.rationale: Pure-helper tests cover payload semantics, while controller tests verify the actual history boundary and lifecycle. Testing only helper output would miss a controller that accidentally appends the untrimmed observation. This supplements the existing runtime suite rather than moving its security and timeout coverage.
alternatives: Test only with a real cloud model, which would make allowance behavior expensive and nondeterministic.
Extend the large existing test_polaris.py file with every new case; a focused test module makes this cross-cutting policy easier to navigate.

"""Pure admission of decoded source characters, separate from I/O and providers."""

import copy


def admit_source(tool_name, observation, remaining_chars):
    """Return (copied result, admitted characters, trimmed by this budget).

    Count only text in built-in read/search observations. Paths, line numbers,
    JSON labels, listings, and other tool results are not source characters.
    This function never mutates the original tool result.
    """
    if type(remaining_chars) is not int or remaining_chars < 0:
        raise ValueError("remaining_chars must be a nonnegative integer")
    result = copy.deepcopy(observation)
    admitted = 0
    trimmed = False

    def take(text):
        nonlocal admitted, trimmed
        excerpt = text[:max(0, remaining_chars - admitted)]
        admitted += len(excerpt)
        trimmed |= len(excerpt) < len(text)
        return excerpt

    if tool_name == "read_file":
        result["text"] = take(result["text"])
    elif tool_name == "search_files":
        matches = []
        for match in result["matches"]:
            original = match["text"]
            text = take(original)
            if text or not original:
                match["text"] = text
                if len(text) < len(original):
                    match["text_truncated"] = True
                matches.append(match)
        result["matches"] = matches
    else:
        return result, 0, False
    result["truncated"] = result.get("truncated", False) or trimmed
    return result, admitted, trimmed

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
from dataclasses import asdict

from . import (
    Config,
    Controller,
    Decision,
    JsonlTrace,
    MockModel,
    OllamaModel,
    ToolCall,
    Workspace,
)


async def run(args):
    model = None
    try:
        config = Config(args.max_decisions, args.model_timeout, args.execution_timeout)
        model = (
            MockModel(
                [
                    Decision(tool_calls=(ToolCall("list_files", {"path": "."}),)),
                    Decision(
                        "Offline demonstration completed; see the tool observation in history."
                    ),
                ]
            )
            if args.mock
            else OllamaModel(args.model, args.api_timeout)
        )
        with Workspace(args.workspace) as workspace:
            result = await Controller(
                model,
                workspace.registry(),
                config,
                JsonlTrace(args.trace) if args.trace else None,
            ).run(args.prompt)
        output = json.dumps(asdict(result), indent=2)
        key = os.getenv("OLLAMA_API_KEY")
        if key:
            # Redact after JSON encoding as keys may contain escaped characters.
            output = output.replace(json.dumps(key)[1:-1], "[REDACTED]")
        print(output)
        return 0 if result.status == "completed" else 1
    except Exception:
        # Never display arbitrary SDK/configuration exceptions, which may carry keys.
        print(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "status": "failed",
                    "failure": {
                        "code": "setup_error",
                        "message": "Check workspace, timeouts, SDK installation, and OLLAMA_API_KEY",
                    },
                }
            )
        )
        return 1
    finally:
        if isinstance(model, OllamaModel):
            await model.aclose()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Polaris read-only workspace agent")
    parser.add_argument("prompt")
    parser.add_argument("--workspace", default=".")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model", default=os.getenv("OLLAMA_MODEL", "gpt-oss:120b-cloud")
    )
    parser.add_argument("--api-timeout", type=float, default=30)
    parser.add_argument("--model-timeout", type=float, default=60)
    parser.add_argument("--execution-timeout", type=float, default=180)
    parser.add_argument("--max-decisions", type=int, default=15)
    parser.add_argument("--trace", help="JSONL metadata trace path (parent must exist)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mock", action="store_true", help="Use deterministic offline demonstration"
    )
    raise SystemExit(asyncio.run(run(parser.parse_args())))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Offline source-admission and controller integration tests."""
import io
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from argparse import Namespace
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

from polaris import Config, Controller, Decision, MockModel, ToolCall, Workspace
from polaris.context_budget import admit_source


def read(path="sample.txt"):
    return ToolCall("read_file", {"path": path})


class AdmissionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_unicode_partial_and_original_is_unchanged(self):
        original = {"text": "a界🙂 \n", "truncated": False}
        result, count, trimmed = admit_source("read_file", original, 3)
        self.assertEqual(result, {"text": "a界🙂", "truncated": True})
        self.assertEqual((count, trimmed), (3, True))
        self.assertEqual(original["text"], "a界🙂 \n")

    def test_exact_zero_and_existing_truncation(self):
        result, count, trimmed = admit_source("read_file", {"text": "ab", "truncated": True}, 2)
        self.assertEqual((count, trimmed, result["truncated"]), (2, False, True))
        result, count, trimmed = admit_source("read_file", {"text": "ab"}, 0)
        self.assertEqual((result["text"], count, trimmed), ("", 0, True))
        self.assertEqual(admit_source("read_file", {"text": ""}, 0)[1:], (0, False))

    def test_search_partial_match_metadata_and_later_matches(self):
        original = {"matches": [{"path": "a", "line": 9, "text": "abcd"},
                                {"path": "b", "line": 10, "text": "efgh"},
                                {"path": "c", "line": 11, "text": "ijkl"}], "truncated": False}
        result, count, trimmed = admit_source("search_files", original, 6)
        self.assertEqual((count, trimmed), (6, True))
        self.assertEqual([m["text"] for m in result["matches"]], ["abcd", "ef"])
        self.assertEqual(result["matches"][1]["line"], 10)
        self.assertTrue(result["matches"][1]["text_truncated"])
        self.assertEqual(original["matches"][1]["text"], "efgh")
        self.assertEqual(admit_source("search_files", original, 0)[0]["matches"], [])

    def test_unrelated_tools_are_not_charged(self):
        value = {"entries": [{"name": "long-path.py", "type": "file"}]}
        self.assertEqual(admit_source("list_files", value, 0), (value, 0, False))

    def test_config_validation(self):
        for value in [0, -1, True, False, 1.5, "100"]:
            with self.subTest(value=value), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                Config(max_source_chars=value)
        self.assertIsNone(Config().max_source_chars)
        self.assertEqual(Config(max_source_chars=1).max_source_chars, 1)


class BudgetRuntimeTests(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_calls(self, calls, budget):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            (Path(directory) / "sample.txt").write_text("needle\n")
            model = MockModel([Decision(tool_calls=tuple(calls)), Decision("done")])
            with Workspace(directory) as workspace:
                result = await Controller(model, workspace.registry(), Config(max_source_chars=budget)).run("inspect")
            observations = [json.loads(m.content) for m in result.history if m.role == "tool"]
            return result, observations, model

    async def test_disabled_mode_preserves_original_envelope(self):
        result, observations, _ = await self.run_calls([read(), read()], None)
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "completed")
        self.assertEqual(observations[0], {"ok": True, "result": {"text": "needle\n", "truncated": False}})
        self.assertEqual(observations[0], observations[1])

    async def test_repeated_reads_share_allowance_and_next_request_is_trimmed(self):
        result, observations, model = await self.run_calls([read(), read(), read()], 10)
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "completed")
        self.assertEqual([o["result"]["text"] for o in observations], ["needle\n", "nee", ""])
        self.assertEqual([o["context_budget"]["consumed_chars"] for o in observations], [7, 10, 10])
        observed = [json.loads(m.content) for m in model.requests[1][0] if m.role == "tool"]
        self.assertEqual(observed, observations)
        self.assertTrue(observed[-1]["context_budget"]["truncated_by_budget"])

    async def test_mixed_read_search_and_non_source_tools(self):
        calls = [read(), ToolCall("search_files", {"query": "needle"}), ToolCall("list_files", {})]
        result, observations, _ = await self.run_calls(calls, 9)
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "completed")
        self.assertEqual(observations[1]["result"]["matches"][0]["text"], "ne")
        self.assertEqual(observations[1]["context_budget"]["remaining_chars"], 0)
        self.assertNotIn("context_budget", observations[2])

    async def test_errors_do_not_consume_allowance(self):
        _, observations, _ = await self.run_calls([read("missing"), read()], 7)
        self.assertEqual(observations[0], {"ok": False, "error": "tool_error"})
        self.assertEqual(observations[1]["context_budget"]["consumed_chars"], 7)
        self.assertFalse(observations[1]["context_budget"]["truncated_by_budget"])

    async def test_controller_reuse_resets_allowance(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            (Path(directory) / "sample.txt").write_text("abc")
            model = MockModel([Decision(tool_calls=(read(),)), Decision("one"),
                               Decision(tool_calls=(read(),)), Decision("two")])
            with Workspace(directory) as workspace:
                controller = Controller(model, workspace.registry(), Config(max_source_chars=2))
                results = [await controller.run("first"), await controller.run("second")]
            for result in results:
                self.assertEqual(result.status, "completed")
                observation = json.loads(next(m.content for m in result.history if m.role == "tool"))
                self.assertEqual(observation["result"]["text"], "ab")
                self.assertEqual(observation["context_budget"]["consumed_chars"], 2)

    async def test_cli_namespace_option_is_forwarded(self):
        from polaris.__main__ import run
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            (Path(directory) / "sample.txt").write_text("abcdef")
            args = Namespace(max_decisions=15, model_timeout=1, execution_timeout=10,
                             mock=True, workspace=directory, trace=None, prompt="inspect",
                             model="unused", api_timeout=1, max_source_chars=3)
            model = MockModel([Decision(tool_calls=(read(),)), Decision("done")])
            output = io.StringIO()
            with patch("polaris.__main__.MockModel", return_value=model), redirect_stdout(output):
                self.assertEqual(await run(args), 0)
            result = json.loads(output.getvalue())
            observation = json.loads(next(m["content"] for m in result["history"] if m["role"] == "tool"))
            self.assertEqual(observation["result"]["text"], "abc")

# Polaris

A small, framework-free Python 3.11+ agent runtime using the official Ollama
Python SDK and direct Ollama Cloud access. Existing miniLLM exercises remain
alongside the `polaris/` package.

The editable coding agent is documented in [simple_agent/README.md](simple_agent/README.md).
The [evaluator study guide](EVALUATOR_STUDY_GUIDE.md) explains the independent
patch evaluator and its agent integration. For a versioned task JSON and trusted
check bundle, run one agent attempt and evaluate it with:

```sh
python -m simple_agent.run_evaluated_agent --task path/to/task.json \
  --checks path/to/check-bundle --output path/to/new-run-directory --model "$OLLAMA_MODEL"
```

This integration executes repository code without a sandbox and is limited to
trusted tasks, checks, and agent output.

For repeated runs over a suite of task definitions, use
`python -m simple_agent.benchmark_suite run --suite suite.json --output runs/first`;
`python -m simple_agent.benchmark_suite compare runs/first runs/second` compares
matching tasks. Independent checks can optionally run in a container; the agent
itself still runs on the host. See the study guide for the suite format and limits.

Its offline trace evaluator reports successes/failures by tool, individual steps,
retries, verification, and latency:

```sh
python -m simple_agent.evaluate --steps
python -m simple_agent.evaluate --format json --output simple_agent/logs/evaluation.json
```

After installing this project, the same CLI is available as `agent-eval`.

## Setup

Secure filesystem tools require Linux or macOS (POSIX descriptor-relative opens).
No local Ollama server is required for direct Cloud access.

```sh
python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e .

# Supply your key via your environment/secret manager. Do not commit it.
export OLLAMA_API_KEY='your-ollama-api-key'
export OLLAMA_MODEL='gpt-oss:120b-cloud'

python -m polaris 'Summarize the Python files in this workspace' \
  --workspace . --model "$OLLAMA_MODEL" \
  --api-timeout 30 --model-timeout 60 --execution-timeout 180
```

Create an API key in your Ollama account and choose a Cloud model with tool
calling support. Model availability depends on your account. See the official
[Cloud setup](https://docs.ollama.com/cloud) and
[Python SDK](https://github.com/ollama/ollama-python#cloud-api-ollamacom).
`OLLAMA_MODEL` or `--model` selects the model. The endpoint is fixed to
`https://ollama.com`; redirects are disabled so credentials stay on that host.

## Offline use and tests

The deterministic mock needs no API key or network. Its demo lists the workspace,
then returns a scripted answer; it does not synthesize a summary.

```sh
python -m polaris 'Inspect this workspace' --workspace . --mock
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Tests use temporary workspaces, scripted decisions, and an in-memory HTTP
transport for the actual SDK. They cover protocol validation, batch preflight,
unknown tools, malformed arguments, traversal, symlinks and symlink replacement,
nonregular files, model/tool errors, output limits, deadlines, decision budgets,
SDK serialization, and trace redaction. Tests require the installed SDK but never
make Cloud requests.

## Runtime behavior

- `model.py`: an async official-SDK adapter and scripted `MockModel`.
- `controller.py`: validation, history, tool dispatch, and execution budgets.
- `types.py`: provider-independent typed decisions, messages, and results.
- `tools.py`: a dataclass-based tool allowlist and workspace file access.
- `trace.py`: metadata-only JSONL execution events with redaction.

`list_files(path=".")` lists one directory. `read_file(path)` reads at most
64 KiB, decoding UTF-8 with replacement. `search_files(query, path=".")` searches
literal, case-sensitive text recursively, with line numbers. Search inspects at
most 1,000 entries and 200 files and returns at most 100 matches; it reads at most
64 KiB per file. Listings are limited to 1,000 entries per directory. Results
include a `truncated` flag when a limit prevents complete output. Unreadable or
nonregular files cause a tool-error observation; symlink entries are skipped in
recursive searches. There are no write or shell tools.

Tool arguments must be objects containing only documented string fields;
unknown fields, missing required fields, empty strings, and strings longer than
4,096 characters are rejected. An entire tool-call batch is validated before
any call executes. Unknown tools or malformed arguments terminate the run.
Known tool failures produce `{ "ok": false, "error": "tool_error" }`
observations so the model can recover. Raw exception messages are never logged
or exposed. Calls execute sequentially, with at most 16 calls per decision.

`Config` defaults to 15 decisions and cannot exceed that ceiling. A decision is
one attempted model request, including a failed request. A final answer on the
15th decision succeeds; requesting more work on the 15th ends with
`decision_budget`. There are no implicit retries. API timeout controls SDK HTTP
operations; model timeout bounds a complete model decision; the overall deadline
includes model calls, tools, and tracing. These are independent configurable
limits, and the earliest applicable limit wins.

Model operations use asyncio cancellation. Built-in tools run in worker threads
and check a monotonic deadline/cancellation flag between bounded operations.
Cancellation cannot interrupt an OS filesystem syscall already in progress;
a stalled network filesystem or an uncooperative custom model/tool is outside
this in-process runtime's hard wall-clock guarantees. Use a local filesystem
and cooperative extensions; process isolation is required for hostile plugins.

Each run returns a `Result` with `status`, `decisions`, `history`, `content`, and
optional `failure` (`code`, `message`). Failure codes are `unknown_tool`,
`invalid_arguments`, `invalid_response`, `model_error`, `model_timeout`,
`execution_deadline`, `decision_budget`, and `trace_error`. CLI setup failures use
`setup_error`. Exit status is 0 on completion, 1 on failure. External cancellation

# Polaris

A small, framework-free Python 3.11+ agent runtime using the official Ollama
Python SDK and direct Ollama Cloud access. Existing miniLLM exercises remain
alongside the `polaris/` package.

The editable coding agent is documented in [simple_agent/README.md](simple_agent/README.md).
The [evaluator study guide](EVALUATOR_STUDY_GUIDE.md) explains the independent
patch evaluator and its agent integration. For a versioned task JSON and trusted
check bundle, run one agent attempt and evaluate it with:

```sh
python -m simple_agent.run_evaluated_agent --task path/to/task.json \
  --checks path/to/check-bundle --output path/to/new-run-directory --model "$OLLAMA_MODEL"
```

This integration executes repository code without a sandbox and is limited to
trusted tasks, checks, and agent output.

For repeated runs over a suite of task definitions, use
`python -m simple_agent.benchmark_suite run --suite suite.json --output runs/first`;
`python -m simple_agent.benchmark_suite compare runs/first runs/second` compares
matching tasks. Independent checks can optionally run in a container; the agent
itself still runs on the host. See the study guide for the suite format and limits.

Its offline trace evaluator reports successes/failures by tool, individual steps,
retries, verification, and latency:

```sh
python -m simple_agent.evaluate --steps
python -m simple_agent.evaluate --format json --output simple_agent/logs/evaluation.json
```

After installing this project, the same CLI is available as `agent-eval`.

## Setup

Secure filesystem tools require Linux or macOS (POSIX descriptor-relative opens).
No local Ollama server is required for direct Cloud access.

```sh
python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e .

# Supply your key via your environment/secret manager. Do not commit it.
export OLLAMA_API_KEY='your-ollama-api-key'
export OLLAMA_MODEL='gpt-oss:120b-cloud'

python -m polaris 'Summarize the Python files in this workspace' \
  --workspace . --model "$OLLAMA_MODEL" \
  --api-timeout 30 --model-timeout 60 --execution-timeout 180
```

Create an API key in your Ollama account and choose a Cloud model with tool
calling support. Model availability depends on your account. See the official
[Cloud setup](https://docs.ollama.com/cloud) and
[Python SDK](https://github.com/ollama/ollama-python#cloud-api-ollamacom).
`OLLAMA_MODEL` or `--model` selects the model. The endpoint is fixed to
`https://ollama.com`; redirects are disabled so credentials stay on that host.

## Offline use and tests

The deterministic mock needs no API key or network. Its demo lists the workspace,
then returns a scripted answer; it does not synthesize a summary.

```sh
python -m polaris 'Inspect this workspace' --workspace . --mock
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Tests use temporary workspaces, scripted decisions, and an in-memory HTTP
transport for the actual SDK. They cover protocol validation, batch preflight,
unknown tools, malformed arguments, traversal, symlinks and symlink replacement,
nonregular files, model/tool errors, output limits, deadlines, decision budgets,
SDK serialization, and trace redaction. Tests require the installed SDK but never
make Cloud requests.

## Runtime behavior

- `model.py`: an async official-SDK adapter and scripted `MockModel`.
- `controller.py`: validation, history, tool dispatch, and execution budgets.
- `types.py`: provider-independent typed decisions, messages, and results.
- `tools.py`: a dataclass-based tool allowlist and workspace file access.
- `trace.py`: metadata-only JSONL execution events with redaction.

`list_files(path=".")` lists one directory. `read_file(path)` reads at most
64 KiB, decoding UTF-8 with replacement. `search_files(query, path=".")` searches
literal, case-sensitive text recursively, with line numbers. Search inspects at
most 1,000 entries and 200 files and returns at most 100 matches; it reads at most
64 KiB per file. Listings are limited to 1,000 entries per directory. Results
include a `truncated` flag when a limit prevents complete output. Unreadable or
nonregular files cause a tool-error observation; symlink entries are skipped in
recursive searches. There are no write or shell tools.

An optional run-wide retrieval allowance is available as `--max-source-chars N`
(or `Config(max_source_chars=N)` programmatically). It is disabled by default.
The controller admits at most N decoded source characters across successful
`read_file` and `search_files` results in one execution. Repeated retrievals are
charged again; whitespace counts, while paths, line numbers, listings, and JSON
metadata do not. The observation includes `context_budget` counts and
`truncated_by_budget`; its existing `truncated` flag remains true for either a
per-tool cap or budget trimming. At exhaustion, source observations contain no
additional text, while final answers and non-source tools remain available.
This allowance is not a tokenizer or a cap on the complete serialized conversation.
It does not prevent filesystem reads. Per-file I/O limits, timeouts, decision
limits, and workspace access checks remain independent.

The offline mock accepts the same configuration without credentials:

```sh
python -m polaris 'Inspect this workspace' --workspace . --mock --max-source-chars 4096
```

read/search admission; the mock CLI command only demonstrates option parsing.

unknown fields, missing required fields, empty strings, and strings longer than

any call executes. Unknown tools or malformed arguments terminate the run.

15th decision succeeds; requesting more work on the 15th ends with

operations; model timeout bounds a complete model decision; the overall deadline

limits, and the earliest applicable limit wins.

Cancellation cannot interrupt an OS filesystem syscall already in progress;
a stalled network filesystem or an uncooperative custom model/tool is outside
this in-process runtime's hard wall-clock guarantees. Use a local filesystem
and cooperative extensions; process isolation is required for hostile plugins.

Each run returns a `Result` with `status`, `decisions`, `history`, `content`, and
